newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arcadia directors reject Sipa bid.
newsitem.headline: Arcadia directors reject Sipa bid.

text.p: Independent directors of Arcadia Minerals NL said on Friday they recommended shareholders reject the takeover bid by gold exploration partner Sipa Resources International NL.
Sipa raised its bid on May 5 to seven Sipa shares and 40 cents cash for every four Arcadia shares from the original five for three scrip offer.
Based on Sipa'a closing price of 58 cents the offer values Arcadia at A$1.115 per share.
Arcadia shares ended at A$1.04 on Friday.
The independent directors said they would not be accepting for their own shares.
They also said that while the independent experts report assessed Sipa's offer to be fair and reasonable, they did not consider the offer to be sufficiently attractive to recommend acceptance.
The directors said they based their recommendation on the view that Sipa would not attract sufficient acceptances to move to compulsory acquisition.
Sipa and Arcadia are partners in the Dublin Hill gold joint venture in Western Australia. The joint venture is 70 percent owned by Sipa and 30 percent by Arcadia.
Sipa shares closed four cents higher at 58 cents.
